page: Microsoft Azure E16-8s_v3 is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance belonging to the ESv3 series. It features 8 dedicated vCPUs driven by an Intel Xeon 8272CL processor running at 2.6 GHz across 4 physical cores with Hyper-Threading. The instance is configured with 128.0 GB of RAM, yielding a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 16 GB per active vCPU. It includes 262 GB of local temporary SSD storage and supports Premium Storage disks under the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor.

In benchmark testing, the E16-8s_v3 exhibits average memory bandwidth, reaching up to 365.97 GB/sec in small block cached reads and 42.22 GB/sec in uncached large block reads. Database and memory operations perform in the average range, demonstrated by PassMark database scores and a Redis SET throughput of 6.25 million operations per second. However, compute-heavy metrics score lower, with single-core and multi-core stress-ng tests placing in the bottom 10% and bottom 25%, respectively. Static web serving reaches 6.32 GB/sec, and LLM inference performance degrades significantly on models larger than 135M parameters.

The E16-8s_v3 offers a cost-effective memory allocation profile by constraining the active vCPU count to 8 while retaining 128.0 GB of memory. This configuration reduces software licensing costs tied to core counts without sacrificing memory capacity. Consequently, the instance is well suited for memory-bound workloads such as medium-sized relational databases, caching tiers like Redis, and in-memory analytics that require substantial RAM relative to processing power.
